metadata.statutory_transition_rule: Under Article 20(1) of the Constitution of India, substantive criminal offences apply prospectively. Offences committed prior to July 1, 2024 continue under IPC; offences on or after July 1, 2024 are registered under BNS. Procedural provisions under BNSS and evidentiary rules under BSA apply as per Supreme Court transition guidelines.

IPC_302.change_notes: Punishment remains death or imprisonment for life and fine. Sub-section (2) introduces mob lynching by 5 or more persons based on race, caste, sex, place of birth, language, religion.

IPC_304.old_title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
IPC_304.new_title: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
IPC_304.change_notes: Divided into intention (imprisonment for life or up to 10 years) and knowledge (up to 10 years).

IPC_304A.new_title: Causing death by negligence (Rash or negligent act)
IPC_304A.change_notes: Imprisonment increased up to 5 years (previously 2 years) and fine. Section 106(2) provides up to 10 years for hit-and-run without reporting.

IPC_304B.change_notes: Death within 7 years of marriage under abnormal circumstances with cruelty/harassment for dowry. Minimum 7 years up to life imprisonment.

IPC_307.change_notes: Substantively identical. Imprisonment up to 10 years, and if hurt caused, life imprisonment or up to 10 years.

IPC_309.new_title: Attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain exercise of lawful power
IPC_309.change_notes: General attempt to suicide is decriminalized; penalized only when done with intent to compel/restrain a public servant from discharging duty.

IPC_323.change_notes: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both.

IPC_325.old_title: Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt
IPC_325.change_notes: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.

IPC_354.old_title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
IPC_354.new_title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage modesty
IPC_354.change_notes: Minimum imprisonment 1 year up to 5 years, and fine.

IPC_354A.old_title: Sexual harassment and punishment for sexual harassment
IPC_354A.change_notes: Physical contact and advances (up to 3 years); sexually coloured remarks (up to 1 year).

IPC_354D.change_notes: First conviction bailable (up to 3 years); second conviction non-bailable (up to 5 years). Covers electronic monitoring.

IPC_375 / 376.change_notes: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years up to life imprisonment. Section 69 also introduces deceitful promises to marry.

IPC_378 / 379.change_notes: Community service introduced as alternative for petty theft under Rs. 5,000 on first conviction upon return of property.

IPC_N/A (Derived from 379).change_notes: New substantive offence specifically addressing snatching of phone, purse, or chain. Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.

IPC_383 / 384.change_notes: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.

IPC_390 / 392.change_notes: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years; if committed on highway between sunset and sunrise, up to 14 years.

IPC_391 / 395.change_notes: Conjoint commission by 5 or more persons. Imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years.

IPC_405 / 406.change_notes: Dishonest misappropriation of entrusted property. Imprisonment up to 5 years (previously 3 years) and fine.

IPC_415 / 420.old_title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
IPC_415 / 420.new_title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
IPC_415 / 420.change_notes: BNS 318(4) corresponds to IPC 420. Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.

IPC_463 / 465.change_notes: Making false document or electronic record. Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.

IPC_498A.old_title: Husband or relative of husband subjecting woman to cruelty
IPC_498A.new_title: Husband or relative subjecting woman to cruelty
IPC_498A.change_notes: BNS Section 85 penalizes cruelty (up to 3 years); Section 86 defines cruelty comprehensively.

IPC_499 / 500.change_notes: Community service introduced as an alternative punishment alongside simple imprisonment up to 2 years or fine.

IPC_503 / 506.change_notes: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine; if threat is of death/grievous hurt, up to 7 years.

IPC_124A.new_title: Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

IPC_141 / 146 / 147.change_notes: Assembly of 5 or more persons with common object. Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine.

IPC_279.old_title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
IPC_279.new_title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
IPC_279.change_notes: Driving endangering human life. Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both.

CrPC_41 / 41A.old_title: When police may arrest without warrant / Notice of appearance
CrPC_41 / 41A.new_title: When police may arrest without warrant
CrPC_41 / 41A.change_notes: Prior permission of Deputy SP required for arresting persons above 60 years or for offences punishable with less than 3 years (with caveats). Notice of appearance integrated.

CrPC_50 / 50A.old_title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and right to bail / Obligation to inform relative
CrPC_50 / 50A.new_title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest / Designated Police Officer
CrPC_50 / 50A.change_notes: Mandates designated police officer at every district and police station to display names and categories of arrested persons.

CrPC_125.old_title: Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
CrPC_125.new_title: Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
CrPC_125.change_notes: Summary statutory remedy for maintenance. Magistrate may order monthly allowance. BNSS retains essence with simplified procedural timelines.

CrPC_144.old_title: Power to issue order in urgent cases of nuisance or apprehended danger
CrPC_144.new_title: Power to issue order in urgent cases of nuisance or apprehended danger
CrPC_144.change_notes: District Magistrate / Sub-divisional Magistrate power. Valid up to 2 months, extendable by State Govt up to 6 months.

CrPC_154.old_title: Information in cognizable cases (First Information Report - FIR)
CrPC_154.new_title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR, Zero FIR & E-FIR)
CrPC_154.change_notes: Statutory recognition of 'Zero FIR' (must register irrespective of jurisdiction and transfer). Expressly authorizes electronic communication (e-FIR) to be signed within 3 days. Preliminary inquiry permitted for offences punishable with 3-7 years within 14 days.

CrPC_160.old_title: Police officer's power to require attendance of witnesses
CrPC_160.new_title: Police officer's power to require attendance of witnesses
CrPC_160.change_notes: Exemption from attending police station extended to persons under 15, over 60 (previously 65), women, and persons with disability/acute illness.

CrPC_161.change_notes: Permits statement recording through audio-video electronic means including mobile phones.

CrPC_164.old_title: Recording of confessions and statements by Magistrate
CrPC_164.change_notes: Audio-video recording permitted. In sexual offences, statement of victim must be recorded by woman Magistrate or in presence of woman.

CrPC_167.old_title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in twenty-four hours (Remand)
CrPC_167.new_title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in 24 hours
CrPC_167.change_notes: Police custody of up to 15 days can now be sought in whole or in parts during the initial 40 or 60 days of the total detention period.

CrPC_100 / 102.new_title: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means
CrPC_100 / 102.change_notes: Mandates audio-video electronic recording (videography) of the entire search and seizure process, including preparation of seizure list without delay.

CrPC_436.old_title: In what cases bail to be taken (Bailable offences)
CrPC_436.new_title: In what cases bail to be taken
CrPC_436.change_notes: Right to bail is absolute in bailable offences upon furnishing surety or personal bond. Indigent persons released on personal recognizance.

CrPC_436A.old_title: Maximum period for which an undertrial prisoner can be detained
CrPC_436A.new_title: Maximum period for which an undertrial prisoner can be detained
CrPC_436A.change_notes: Major relief: A first-time offender (never previously convicted of any offence) shall be released on bond/bail after serving one-third of the maximum imprisonment period.

CrPC_437.old_title: When bail may be taken in case of non-bailable offence
CrPC_437.new_title: When bail may be taken in non-bailable offence
CrPC_437.change_notes: Discretion of Magistrate. Proviso allows bail to women, sick, infirm, or persons under 16.

CrPC_438.old_title: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest (Anticipatory Bail)
CrPC_438.new_title: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest
CrPC_438.change_notes: Sessions Court and High Court retain anticipatory bail jurisdiction. Clarifications on conditions regarding presence at interrogation.

CrPC_439.old_title: Special powers of High Court or Court of Session regarding bail
CrPC_439.new_title: Special powers of High Court or Court of Session regarding bail
CrPC_439.change_notes: Concurrent power of Sessions Court and High Court for regular bail and cancellation of bail.

CrPC_482.old_title: Saving of inherent powers of High Court
CrPC_482.new_title: Saving of inherent powers of High Court
CrPC_482.change_notes: High Court's inherent jurisdiction to prevent abuse of process of any court or secure ends of justice (quashing FIRs, criminal complaints).
